newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Australia confident about ASEAN economies.
newsitem.headline: Australia confident about ASEAN economies.

text.p: Australia said on Monday it remained upbeat about Southeast Asian economies despite concerns that currency turmoil had dented the region's dynamic growth.
"The Australian government has every confidence about the fundamental strength of the ASEAN economies," Australian Foreign Minister Alexander Downer told a news briefing.
"The problems in Thailand recently...has had a ripple effect but what I must say overall we have every confidence (in ASEAN economies)," he said.
Thailand is facing its worst economic growth in a decade, and had to devalue its baht.
Downer has been in Malaysia since Friday for meetings between the nine-member Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) and its 10 so-called dialogue partners of Western and Asian powers.
Speculators have been blamed for sharp selloffs in Southeast Asia's currencies.

ASEAN said in the closing statement for its 30th ministerial meetings that there were well coordinated efforts to destabilise the region's currencies, which were threatening the stability of all ASEAN economies.
Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad has gone further in his cricitisms, saying speculators had wrecked decades of development in the region.
Mahathir has singled out U.S. financier George Soros as a speculator in regional currencies. Soros has denied the allegations.

Downer said Australia was following the situation in Southeast Asia with keen interest. "ASEAN economies are very big economic partners of ours and any speculation against ASEAN economies or any weakening of ASEAN economies will be a matter of great concern to Australia," he said on Monday.
